name: Lamborghini Sián FKP 37
instructions: omr/instructions/42115-1-1.pdf and omr/instructions/42115-1-2.pdf (two books, six build boxes: 1 gearbox and rear suspension, 2 engine and front suspension, 3 interior and seats, 4 rear spoiler, 5 scissor doors, 6 wheels; no single functions page, so functions are read from the build steps' arrows and the photos)

functions.does: Pushed along, all four wheels drive together through a differential on each axle, and in gear the V12 turns: its twelve pistons run up and down in their two banks.
functions.source: book 1: steps 1-180 (gearbox, rear differential, pages 30-130), steps 187-215 (V12 and crankshaft, pages 140-160), front axle and its differential (box 2); the photos on pages 139 and 224
functions.note: whether the front wheels are driven too is inferred from the front differential p797; the gearbox must be in a gear for the engine to turn

functions.does: The paddle shifters behind the steering wheel change gear in the eight-speed sequential gearbox: each pull of a paddle turns the selector one step, which turns two changeover rotary catches through knob gears to slide the gearbox's driving rings in turn.
functions.source: book 1: pages 104-105 (step 134: the insets show the changeover catches and the driving rings), the paddle shifter submodel (box 1, around page 120); 8 speeds from the set's description, not drawn in the book
functions.note: how many paddle pulls give each gear, and which paddle shifts up, are inferred: the owner should check. The ring p211 18947 should slide as the catches turn

functions.does: The lever on the centre console between the seats switches the gearbox between drive and neutral (or reverse): its towball top turns a changeover catch that slides a driving ring on the shaft to the gearbox.
functions.source: inferred: the changeover catch p1081, its towball p1082 and the driving ring p549 sit together on the centre line in front of the gearbox
functions.note: what this lever selects is not shown in the pages read; the owner should check

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the front wheels: its column turns through universal joints and gears down to a pinion on the steering rack.
functions.source: book 1: box 2 (front axle and steering rack), box 3 (the column and wheel); the photo on page 259

functions.does: All four wheels have independent pushrod suspension: each wheel's wishbones push a rocker that compresses a pair of shock absorbers lying across the car.
functions.source: book 1: pages 94-98 (step 127: the yellow arrows show the rear wishbones swinging), box 2 (front suspension); the 'Engine & front suspension' page 138

functions.does: The shock absorbers' springs hold the car up and spring back.
functions.source: book 1: steps building the four pairs of shock absorbers
functions.skip: springs only matter under gravity or force

functions.does: The rear spoiler rises and tilts: a lever in the interior pushes a flexible axle, used as a push rod, back to the spoiler lift under the engine cover, whose yellow axles push the wing up.
functions.source: book 1: pages 299-304 (steps 462-471: a lever with a curved yellow arrow, fitted in the chassis), page 315 (step 491, a second lever); book 2: pages 37-39 (steps 555-563: the spoiler lift, the yellow arrow pushing its axle), the 'Rear spoiler' page 54 and the photo on page 55
functions.note: which lever raises the spoiler, and how the flexible axles carry the push, are inferred from the pages read: the owner should name the control. p2680 and p2681 are the wing's pivots

functions.does: The two scissor doors swing up and forward on hinges at their front edges.
functions.source: book 2: box 5 (pages 188-300), the 'Scissor doors' page 190 and the photo on page 191

functions.does: The front hood lifts, showing the luggage space and the set's bag.
functions.source: book 2: box 5, step 1078 (page 320: the hood shown open) and the hood submodel

functions.does: The engine cover behind the cabin lifts to show the V12.
functions.source: book 2: box 4, rear hood submodel; inferred that it opens from its hinge pins and the engine photos
inferred: the seat submodels (book 1, steps 395-447) are pinned to the floor on axles; the book's arrows weren't checked for them
functions.note: unsure whether the seats move at all: the owner should check
